$about: The align-engine manifest (standard ADR-005). The align/update/self-verify skills read THIS to know what an aligned repo must have - instead of hardcoding it in prose or JS. Paths are the client layout - identical to the standard/ tree in this repo. since names the release that first shipped an entry; unreleased rides the next cut. An aligned repo carries a copy of this file matching the state it last aligned to (a bookmark, never a version it stays at - standard ADR-025); `scripts/self-verify.mjs` checks the repo against it and reports drift as a number. Method docs are adopted BY REFERENCE, never copied: the `references` section names them at their home in the standards repo (standard ADR-004/023) - self-verify notes them, checks no files. The top-level `profile` field (core|scale, standard ADR-011) ships set to `scale` - check everything - and align rewrites it in the repo's copy from the intake's answer; self-verify and the shipped CI gate both read it, and both fall back to `scale` when it is missing, so a copy that lost the field is checked at the stricter tier rather than the looser one and self-verify says the field is absent instead of defaulting in silence. The normative source is SPEC.md; each entry cites the rule it enforces (`rule`). Two fields say what the entry's CONTENT must be, because existence alone is close to no check for the entries whose content is the standard's own: a `copy` entry carries `sha256` - a hash string for a file, one hash per member for a directory - generated by tools/manifest-hashes.mjs and verified by tools/tree-check.mjs, never hand-written, and self-verify hashes the local file against it (CRLF normalized to LF; the manifest itself carries none, since a file cannot hold its own hash; a member missing from a directory entry is reported the same way a changed one is, so a required item quietly removed is a content failure, not a silent pass); a `merge` entry, which is adapted on purpose and so cannot be hashed, MAY declare `requiredKeys` - dotted key paths that must be present in the merged result (JSON objects and YAML block mappings; presence only, never a value). A deliberate, recorded deviation goes in `exceptions`: { "kind": "file"|"section"|"content"|"key", "match": "<path>" for a file or its content, "<file>#<heading>" for a section, "<file>#<key.path>" for a key, "reason": "..." } - self-verify.mjs reports it as excepted rather than drift (R17), keeps it in the adoption denominator so excepting can never raise the percentage, and prints the count in the summary. The hatch is bounded: there is no `guard` kind (a guard is a live check - waiving its verdict removes it instead of recording a deviation from it), a guard's own script file cannot be excepted by `kind: "file"` (a missing guard script is skipped, so that would disable a blocking check at drift 0 - use `kind: "content"`, which keeps the guard running), and an exception with no `reason` is not a recorded one. `provenanceCommit` (standard ADR-052) is the standards repo's full commit SHA this repo's copy last aligned to - ships `null`, and `align-to-standards`/`update-to-latest` write it on every successful run; it is what the delta is computed from, `.standards-version` staying the human-facing bookmark it already was. `removedPaths` (standard ADR-052) is an append-only list of `{ path, since, note }` for paths the standard has removed - hand-maintained at release time like CHANGELOG.md, never generated from a tree diff; self-verify fails a repo that still has a listed path on disk, waivable only through `exceptions` like any other drift.

adaptRules.copy: ship verbatim; the repo gets a byte-for-byte copy (guards, templates that carry no repo-specific content)
adaptRules.merge: combine the standard's content with what the repo already has, keeping both (ignore files, CI that already has jobs)
adaptRules.fill-from-repo: scaffold the shell from the standard, then author the body from THIS repo's reality - never blind-copy the example prose (ARCHITECTURE, PRODUCT, specs)
adaptRules.reference: do not copy; link to the living standard - always latest (standard ADR-004/025 - the standard's own decisions reach clients by reference)

files.purpose: the single agent entry point
the state this repo last aligned to - a bookmark the delta is measured from, never a version to stay at (standard ADR-025); written by align-to-standards / update-to-latest
this manifest, matching the recorded state - what self-verify checks against
the normative core this manifest projects - readable in place
the file Claude Code loads first - points at AGENTS.md and carries the rule to check the skills before acting (R1); a non-Claude repo carries the same content in whatever its agent loads first
the ADR/BDR decision log
pre-decision ideas - status-driven, graduate into records/specs on approval (standard ADR-010)
discovery dossiers - provenance-stamped extracts per topic, never normative (standard ADR-024)
living capability specs
capability -> code globs, so the coupling guard can bind spec to code
the work ledger; items leave only when their DoD is met
where a closed row goes, with a `where` cell naming what its content became; ships empty, and a repo that has closed nothing deletes it until the first row moves (standard ADR-051)
the only home of history (standard ADR-018); a PR describes its change under `## Unreleased` and never touches the version - R18's one path, at every profile
the verify step - checks the repo against this manifest
spec layout guard
a fact restated in prose still agrees with its source - declared homes and claims (R4)
the facts this repo restates: one home each, every restatement declared

the shape of a declared fact, reference only - do not rename or copy its placeholder content into docs/facts.json; write docs/facts.json from scratch, in this shape, once this repo has its first fact worth declaring (R4)
the DDL under database/schema/ and its typed twin stay 1:1 - the declared edge resolves and every name is covered
the ADR/BDR README index and the files on disk agree - no duplicate id, nothing indexed that is not there, nothing there that is not indexed
the Gate 2 and Gate 5 artifacts carry what the gate is for - eight passes rated, the scope block's total equal to the sum of its categories, an owner role on every alignment item
the lifecycle skills - the standard as executable procedures (Claude reference form; a non-Claude repo ports them to its agent's own mechanism)
the spec engine runtime the skills invoke (gate, setup, templates, MIT licence)
what more than one guard needs - glob matching, so two guards cannot answer the same question differently
secret-scan config (the shipped scan SHOULD gate CI)
the secret-scan workflow template
weekly notification that a newer standard exists - opens one issue per release, never edits the recorded state (standard ADR-025)
agent settings baseline - permission lists, and which guards run
forces LF on the shipped bash guards and Node scripts - a repo whose own setting is eol=crlf makes every hook exit 127 with empty stdout, which for a deny-guard is silence, not a refusal
the pre-execution guards themselves - remote-DB writes, force-push, CI secrets - behind one dispatcher that denies when any of them is missing or broken
drives every guard with real commands - they only emit output on a denial, so a broken guard is otherwise silent
the altitude apex R1 names - optional but expected
code<->spec coupling guard (+ --audit) - the tool ships at core, the blocking CI gate is scale (R11)
the CI workflow that wires self-verify + both guards - how R16's gate actually runs
the persona roster the R10 gate checks specs against - without it the gate has nothing to hold
what Step 0 measured and asked before any align work proceeded - the record that makes intake checkable, not just performed (standard ADR-042)
what Gate 2's eight-pass assessment found - maturity per pass, top risks, findings grouped by the owner role that must act; the evidence Gate 5's count is derived from (standard ADR-048)
the repo's front door - authored from this repo's reality
contribution mechanics pointer - defers to AGENTS.md
vulnerability-reporting contact and posture (placeholders filled at adoption)
exact runtime version for the dependency-free guards and CI setup
PR template - what/why, decision-record impact across both streams, test plan, checklist
the docs hub table
how it is built - the altitude names it (filled from this repo)
what it is and where it is going (filled from this repo)
canonical conventions block - merged into AGENTS.md at adoption
event-taxonomy tracking plan template
per-persona journey maps coupled to capabilities
anonymized research studies feeding personas, ideas and specs
operational runbooks + postmortems - agent-followable at 3 a.m.
work sprints - what a team committed to and by when; an intent is in the pool or in exactly one sprint (standard ADR-028)
proves the one-place invariant the pool and the sprints depend on
a closed row reached the archive with a pointer to what its content became, instead of being deleted (standard ADR-051)

renders the work state - pool, sprints, timeline, records, changelog - as one static page for the people who never open the repository; index.mjs is the generator, src/ the page and password-gate material it inlines. A projection, never a second place work is tracked
builds the dashboard manually (workflow_dispatch); publishes it only when the repository is public or the build is locked with a password, because Pages on a private repository is served publicly
the points this standard must ask a person about - question, answers in order, permitted provenance and the paths each one gates
refuses a write to a gated artifact until that point's question actually fired - read from the transcript structurally, so prose about having asked does not count
what became of every answer: state, who, when, where it landed, and the backlog row carrying a deferred one

the provenance ledger stays honest - every required point has a row, a deferred answer names a backlog row that exists, and a point stops being legally pending once something it gates has been written; and the guard itself reached a commit before any Gate artifact it protects did

references.purpose: where each kind of knowledge lands (ends 'ADR or rule?')
the forks every repo consciously decides, with paved-road defaults
the gated path from unaligned to aligned + the modernize pass
the read-only assessment the transition agent runs, and the periodic health check
how work flows around the spec (PO -> dev -> AI)
the two-outputs changelog model teams follow
real situations -> the prompt -> what the standard does (specs day to day)
discovery dossiers: from a meeting to a spec with provenance (standard ADR-024)
evidence-checked practices for driving the agent: context, verification, review load, blast radius
what drift 0 does and does not certify - the tiers, the flags, the arithmetic
what must be installed before an agent starts an adoption
the axes a repo decides once - a menu, answered in your own security ADR
how to write a capability spec - the tiers, the contracts, what makes buildable checkable (R8, R9)
the ADR/BDR streams, the record test and the altitude hierarchy (R5)
what the agent starts on its own, what it refuses, and what it never decides for you
the dev's job when building: intent in, a buildable spec plus its records out
rolling the standard out across more than one repo, consistently
the product owner's job: what should be true, and for whom
the three files that answer what is still owed, what is happening now, and when it lands
the OPTIONAL tracker-sync extension - a per-capability sidecar core never reads; skip it entirely if you sync to no tracker (standard ADR-032)
language is a configuration, not a constraint - the reasoning and the guidance for a non-English team

sections.heading: Altitude
sections.purpose: the precedence order wins-on-conflict must be stated

sections.heading: Unreleased
sections.purpose: R18/R25 - a PR describes its change here; nothing else holds history, and drift 0 must not be reachable with no changelog at all

sections.heading: The loop runs itself (unprompted)
sections.purpose: the unprompted-behaviour contract survives deletion or a thin rewrite - it is what makes the loop self-triggering rather than merely documented

sections.heading: Volunteer, don't wait to be asked
sections.purpose: an ambiguous mention of a bug, a decision, or scope creep gets named and asked about, not silently actioned or silently dropped

sections.heading: Say where you are
sections.purpose: long work reports itself every 60-120 seconds - what is happening and what it is waiting on - and never invents progress or a result that has not come back

guards.purpose: spec files are where and shaped as the standard requires
declared facts still agree with their source (skips itself where none are declared)
the schema and its typed twin have not drifted (skips itself where there is no database)
domain code changed without touching its spec fails CI
an intent is in the backlog pool or in exactly one sprint (skips itself where there are no sprints)
the ADR/BDR index and the directory on disk agree - duplicate id, orphaned index row, or unindexed record all fail

the two gate artifacts carry what the gate is for - eight passes rated, the scope block adds up, every alignment item owned (skips itself where no assessment exists, which self-verify already reports)
a row removed from the pool reached the archive, and every archived row names where its content went (skips its archive checks where nothing has been archived yet)
the record of who answered what is present and internally consistent, and the guard that produced it landed before any Gate artifact it protects did

decisions.prompt: Where are the module/domain seams? (slice by capability, not layer)
Test tiers and where each runs?
The floor below which nothing ships?

specs.tierDecision: Could an agent rebuild and verify this capability from the spec alone, without reading the code? If yes -> buildable; behavioral is an escape hatch that must be justified in-spec and stays rare.

removedPaths.note: renamed to .claude/skills/update-to-latest - the target was always latest, never a pin (standard ADR-025/052); nothing to migrate, the replacement ships in the same release

moved to skills/record-run/ in the standards repo - a transition skill run from a checkout, never shipped into the client tree (standard ADR-045's correction, ADOPT-DEFAULTS-1); nothing in the adopted repo replaces it, delete the directory on update
